title: Puerto Rico: review the dealer relationship before promising a territory
description: Law 75 can make the actual distribution or service role matter to renewal, changes and exit.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A contract label does not settle the Puerto Rico relationship
paragraphs: Puerto Rico’s official Spanish Law 75 consolidation defines distribution agreements by the relationship actually established. Its definition includes taking real responsibility for goods distribution or service provision by concession or franchise in the Puerto Rico market. The management task is to describe what the local party will actually build and operate, then assess whether that relationship falls within the law.

In the official consolidated text reviewed here, Article 2 addresses termination, impairment and nonrenewal without just cause, even where a contract reserves a unilateral exit. This is a reason to examine the relationship before making changes; it is not a verdict that every franchise is a protected dealer or that every exit is unlawful.

sections.heading: Fictional B2B example: a maintenance partner develops key accounts
paragraphs: A European industrial-maintenance brand appoints a Puerto Rico partner to develop accounts, recruit a service team and support installed equipment. Two years later, the brand wants to reserve the largest account for direct service. Before issuing a notice, the COO documents who created the account, existing allocation terms, actual service responsibilities and the proposed change.

The team should not treat this as merely changing a sales spreadsheet. Article 2A describes specific impairment presumptions and qualifications. Counsel needs the actual conduct, contract and market evidence. A court remedy or damages award is not an automatic repayment of every investment.

sections.heading: Prepare the relationship-change file
bullets: Expansion lead: list the local party’s market-development, customer, stock, service and investment responsibilities.
COO: preserve actual performance, service quality, complaints and any cure discussions.
Commercial lead: identify exclusivity, national accounts, direct sales and proposed allocation changes.
Relationship adviser: assess dealer status, just cause and current controlling cases before an appointment, nonrenewal, impairment or termination.
CFO: identify investments and costs actually committed to this relationship; do not insert statutory damage factors as a forecast.

sections.heading: Keep the other territorial workstreams open
paragraphs: Federal § 436.2 expressly includes a franchise to be located in U.S. territories, subject to its exemptions. That federal location rule does not decide independent territorial definitions, registration/notice obligations, relationship protections, tax or operating permissions.

Puerto Rico is inside the U.S. customs territory under 19 CFR§ 101.1. That fact does not determine local excise/sales taxes, a product’s origin or customs classification. Operating permits, entity qualification, employment and people-mobility questions remain separate.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
paragraphs: The government PDF is a Spanish consolidation revised 13 November 2020; this English explanation is an AI-assisted summary. Current case law, any later amendments and the facts defining a protected dealer need review. The PDF’s forum/arbitration language must also be assessed against applicable federal law and controlling decisions; this guide does not declare every out-of-territory arbitration clause invalid.

practicalOutput: A documented local relationship and a change/renewal decision file.
limitations: This guide covers named issues only. It does not establish that an offer, sale, work assignment, import or opening is authorised. Local, sector and current transaction-specific questions remain to be reviewed.

title: U.S. Virgin Islands: build the operating-license evidence chain
description: Separate the local operator, its premises reviews and any professional permissions from the franchise-sales analysis.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the entity, activity and island
paragraphs: DLCA’s official steps identify several records that can be needed before a business license is issued: entity/trade-name registration, initial tax-clearance, police review, zoning and applicable fire, health and board certification. Some reviews are conducted electronically on the applicant’s behalf. A license application is not evidence that the reviews have cleared.

Identify the actual operating entity and site on St. Thomas, St. Croix or St. John and the precise service. A professional or construction activity can require a board workstream in addition to the ordinary business license.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a facilities operator includes HVAC work
paragraphs: A local partner offers cleaning plus heating, ventilation and air-conditioning maintenance. The team separates ordinary cleaning from the technician’s mechanical work rather than assuming one brand license covers both. DLCA specifically lists mechanical/HVAC professions among its board-certification categories; the actual personnel, scope and current board rules need checking.

The premises lead records which fire or health review applies to the actual location. A health inspection is not added automatically to every service operation merely because it appears in a general licensing list.

rows: Current initial or renewal instructions and confirmation

paragraphs: DLCA’s page says renewal applicants receive a license without confirmation of tax clearance, while remaining responsible for current tax obligations and possible later action. Do not use that renewal instruction to assume initial applications have no tax-clearance workstream.

title: Guam: separate foreign-company authority from a service operating license

reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: An off-island company has two distinct questions
paragraphs: 18 GCA§ 7102(a) says a foreign corporation must obtain both a business license and a certificate of authority before transacting business in Guam. The same section lists activities that, alone, are not transacting business. Map the proposed facts before deciding whether the foreign parent, a local subsidiary, the partner or more than one entity has a qualification task.

A company based in a U.S. state is still off-island for this corporate-law question. Conversely, owning a subsidiary alone is not automatically treated as the parent transacting business under the cited section. This distinction does not decide tax nexus or franchise classification.

sections.heading: The service category matters
paragraphs: 11 GCA Chapter 76 describes annual service licensing for covered non-professional service activity, excluding services an employee renders to the employer from that description. Section 76103 separately addresses services licensed under other provisions. Identify a licensed profession or trade before choosing the general-service route.

Chapter 70’s general license rule and the Business License and Permit Center’s agency resources are additional leads. Site, environmental, fire, health and sector questions must be mapped for the actual operation; the agency directory is not a list of permits every business must obtain.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a Singapore maintenance brand
paragraphs: The Singapore parent trains a Guam partner and sends a technical manager for commissioning. The local company intends to employ technicians, store equipment and repair customer systems. Record the parent’s activities, the partner’s activities, each premises and each person’s actual work separately. title: CNMI: license each business line and location, then test staffing dependencies

reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A business line and a site are separate inputs
paragraphs: 4 CMC§ 5611 requires a license before engaging in or continuing a business. It calls for one general business license for each business line at each Commonwealth location; licenses have a one-year term and are nontransferable. Fees are established by regulation, so an unknown application cost is not zero.

The Registrar’s official document list separately covers domestic and foreign entity registration, including foreign-company authority/good-standing documents. Registration of the entity does not substitute for a Finance business license.

sections.heading: Fictional example: one partner, two islands and two activities

The team names customer sites separately from business locations and asks how the actual operating pattern is classified. A commercial region or a master-franchise territory map does not answer that administrative question.

sections.heading: Staffing can be an early feasibility dependency
paragraphs: The DOL’s CW-1 program page describes a CNMI employer route with prevailing-wage, labor-certification and U.S. worker recruitment requirements. The employer needs approved temporary labor certification before the separate USCIS petition. This route is not a generic promise that overseas staff can be moved to the mainland or Guam.

For a management-run service business, test the local recruiting plan and manager cost first. If a named overseas specialist is essential, put the unresolved work-authorisation path before a delivery commitment.

sections.heading: Do not collapse three approvals into one

It separately directs corporations to business licensing before transacting business. The correct route depends on entity type; the checklist identifies exceptions to that named foreign-corporation law.

Commerce also says activity, location and citizenship can affect regulation by different agencies, boards and commissions. Its current page gives a calendar-year business-license expiry and an October 1–December 31 renewal period.

sections.heading: Ownership can change the licensing route

These administrative provisions must be read with statutory definitions and any subsequent changes. The site does not decide an applicant’s American Samoan, residency or other legal status.

title: A U.S. territory is not always inside the U.S. customs territory

reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the defined boundary

The definition does not tell you a duty rate, commodity classification, admissibility or tax amount. Nor does it decide the rules for shipping goods from a territory into the mainland.
